full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the instant civil review petition, are that the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 35 of 1983 before the Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Khulna (the suit was finally heard and disposed of as Title Suit No. 61 of 1990) for setting aside the certificate sale held on 24.09.1980 in Certificate Case No.07/B.K.B/79-80. It was stated, inter alia, that 11.58 acres land recorded in CS Khatian No. 217 of Mouza-Krishnanagar under PS Batiaghata within District-Khulna belonged to Binod Bihari Golder and his other co-sharers. Then, a rent decree against the tenants of the holding recorded in CS Khatina No. 217 including Binod Bihari Golder was put to execution in Rent Execution Case No. 85 of 1961 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Khulna by the landlords of the holding where one of the judgment-debtors, Binod Bihari Golder, actively participated in the rent execution case to evade payment of the decretal amount. Then, other attempts having failed, Binod Bihari Golder filed objection under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908(the Code), which also ultimately failed and finally the entire holding of CS Khatian No. 217 was put into auction. Then, one Kazi Shamsujjoha purchased the entire holding in open auction on 16.12.1963. Ultimately, the same was confirmed, and auction purchaser Kazi Shamsujjoha was put into possession of the entire 11.58 acres land through Court on 06.08.1964. Thereafter, Kazi Shamsujjoha mutated his name in the SA Khatian and had been paying rents to the Government regularly and possessing and enjoying the said land by cultivating sometimes through Borgader and some-times under his own plough with hired labourers. In the middle part of November 1982, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 threatened the petitioners that they would cut away the paddy from the case land disclosing that they purchased 5.06 acres land in certificate sale held on 24.09.1980 vide Certificate Case No. 07/B.K./79-80. Then, on an enquiry, the plaintiffs came to know that said Binod Bihari Golder mortgaged 5.06 acres land out of 11.58 acres to the then Krishi Bank for loan of taka 1700.00 by a mortgage deed dated 13.11.1962. In these circumstances, the plaintiffs were constrained to institute the suit. 

 3. Defendant-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable and that the same was barred by limitation. Their definite case was that the suit land originally belonged to Anarullah Shaikh, Danesh Shaikh, Abdullah Shaikh and Wazeruddin Shaikh to the extent of 2 annas 8 gondas shares each and Fedullah Shaikh and Rahman Shaikh to the extent of 3 annas 4 gondas share each out of total area of 12.16 acres land under the then landlady Hemanta Kumari Debi. The said superior interest of the suit jote of Hemanta Kumari Debi was never sold to Anisuzzaman and another who had no rent receiving interest and as such they had no authority to file Rent Suit No. 59 of 1952 in the Court of Munsif, Khulna. The heirs of Anarullah Shaikh sold their interest to Binod Bihari Golder, who was in possession of the suit land. Hironmoy Roy also acquired some interest in the suit Jama and he transferred the same on 12.03.1952 to one Bashir. Further case of the defendants was that the plaintiffs had no authority to purchase the share of Binod Bihari and Hironmoy. Neither the right, title and interest of Binod Bihari nor that of Kalipada and others passed in the auction sale as claimed by the plaintiffs. While the suit land was in the khas possession of Binod Bihari, he paid rent to the Government and 5.06 acres land of CS Khatian No. 217 was mortgaged to the then Agricultural Development Bank, Khulna vide Loan Case No.745/61-62 dated 30.11.1962 from which he took loan of taka 1700.00. The said mortgage loan amount was not paid in time, for which the Manager of the said Bank sent the case to the Certificate Officer, Khulna Sadar, for starting Certificate Case No. 7/B.K.B/79- 80 for realisation of taka 9,593.00 in total including interest. The suit land was put to auction and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in open auction purchased the suit land and took delivery of possession on 30.10.1980. The defendants got their names mutated and they paid rent to the Government and since then the defendants had been possessing the suit land through Bargader. They also stated that neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor got possession over the suit land. The plaintiffs claimed unspecified land on the basis of so-called sale certificate filed by the plaintiffs and, as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 7. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the petitioners got certified copy of the judgment dated 19.12.1957 passed in Second Appeal No.476 of 1954 on 15.04.2015 and therefore, it could not be produced earlier to remove doubt as to the genuineness of the decree passed in Rent Suit No.59 of 1952 and for these reasons the impugned judgment was required to be reviewed. He further submitted that the judgment in Second Appeal No. 476 of 1954 showed that the question of landlord and tenant relationship was considered earlier and was finally decided by judgment and decree dated 16.06.1959 dismissing the present suit questioning the right of Anisuzzaman Khandoker and others for filing the rent suit. He further submitted that the suit was dismissed holding that the auction sale in Rent Execution Case No. 85 of 1961 was not permissible in law after acquisition of rent receiving interest. But by section 68C of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, right to institute and continue the rent suit and the rent execution case was given afresh which was not taken into consideration. He further submitted that after auction filing of Rent Execution Case No. 85 of 1961, judgment-debtor, Binod Behari Golder, contested the case by filing Objection Miscellaneous Case No. 220 of 1961 and Miscellaneous Appeal No. 16 of 1962 and thereafter, 11.58 acres land was sold in auction which was brushed aside only on suspicion. He further submitted that delay in mutating name by the auction purchaser was taken into consideration for disbelieving auction purchase dated 11.11.1963 by Kazi Shamsujjoha. But filing Title Suit No. 639 of 1966 by judgment-debtor, Binod Behari Golder, Miscellaneous Case No. 126 of 1966 for setting aside sale, Miscellaneous Case No. 18 of 1968 for setting aside the ex-perte order setting aside sale and continuance of litigation up to 16.10.1969 was not taken into consideration. He further submitted that the decision in the case of Abdul Hamid and others-Vs-Ali Baksh Mondol and others reported in 20 DLR 699 was a judgment per in curiam in view of the provision of section 68C of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. He further submitted that the investigation report in C.R. Case No.4029 of 2009 found that the certificate sale of 5.06 acres land in Certificate Case No.7BKB/79-80 was totally false. The petitioners proved their title and possession by producing registered certificate of sale of land, writ of delivery of possession, series of registered barga kabuliyat, order of mutation of name in SA Khatian and payment of rent to Government continuously for more than 25 years by producing series of rent receipts, but these evidence was not at all considered at any stage.
